# `metrics.interval_s`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Interval in seconds between two background runs of the metrics exporter that exposes Prometheus metrics.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `10` |
| Available since | 1.0 |
| Component | metrics |
| Unit | s |
| Default changed | in 3.0 (see release notes) |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `metrics.interval_s` only if you observe problems with the metrics exporter that exposes Prometheus metrics, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[metrics]
interval_s = 10
```

# `pq topic restore`

> CLI reference, PaderQueue 4.x

Restores a topic.

## Usage
```
pq topic restore <name> [flags]
```

## Flags
| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--retain-days` | Number of days the result is kept before it is deleted automatically. |
| `--tenant` | Name of the tenant the command applies to. |

## Example
```
pq topic restore orders --retain-days
```

# `pq topic describe`

> CLI reference, PaderQueue 4.x

Describes a topic.

## Usage
```
pq topic describe <name> [flags]
```

## Flags
| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | Show what would happen without changing anything. |
| `--since` | Only consider objects created after this timestamp (ISO 8601). |
| `--tenant` | Name of the tenant the command applies to. |
| `--timeout` | Seconds to wait for the operation to finish. Default: 30. |

## Example

pq topic describe orders --dry-run

- T+22: On-call engineer found PQ-E1915 in the broker logs.
- T+45: The team rolled back the last client deployment.
- T+90: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a marketing campaign that tripled traffic.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E1915.
